question: Who was the first Indian poet who was invited to record his poems at the Library of Congress in Washington DC?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Abhay K.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Abhay K was the first Indian poet to be invited to record his poems at the prestigious** Library of Congress** in **Washington, D.C.**
 
• He is not only a **poet **but also a **diplomat**, serving in various Indian embassies, enhancing his global literary presence.
 
• Abhay K is well-known for writing the **"Earth Anthem,"** which promotes environmental awareness and is translated into several languages.
 
• He has been awarded the **SAARC** Literary Award for his contribution to South Asian poetry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ravindra Bhattacharya:**

 
 
• Ravindra Bhattacharya is an Indian poet and literary **critic** known for his works in Hindi and Bengali.
 
• He has contributed significantly to Indian literature but was not invited to the Library of Congress.
 
 
 
• **Gopalakrishna Adiga:**
 
 
• A prominent Kannada poet and a major figure in modern Kannada literature, often regarded as the '**pioneer of modern Kannada poetry**.'
 
• Though influential in Indian literature, he was not the first Indian poet invited to the Library of Congress.
 
 
 
• **Vinay Kumar:**
 
 
• An Indian poet known for his work in contemporary **Hindi literature.**
 
• He has made significant contributions to Hindi poetry but has no record of being invited to the Library of Congress.
